rd.heading: Research and Development Activities
rd.text:
Spectral plans to continue investing in research and development, with an emphasis on applied technologies that have potential commercial relevance to its operating businesses or target markets. R&D activities are expected to focus on software development, algorithm design, data analytics, and automation tools, rather than speculative or purely theoretical research. Management intends to allocate R&D resources in a disciplined manner, balancing innovation objectives with the need to manage costs and achieve near- and medium-term operational goals.

Certain research initiatives may involve emerging or experimental technologies, including quantum-inspired or hybrid computing approaches. These initiatives are exploratory in nature and may require substantial additional development, validation, and investment before they can be commercialized, if at all. The Company’s plan of operations does not assume that any specific R&D initiative will result in commercially viable products.

The total for the three months ended September 30, 2026 includes a non-cash loss of $1,478 from the change in fair value of contingent consideration and $494 in net interest expense related to the accounts receivable financing facilities and other obligations. Total other income for the three months ended September 30, 2025 consisted of other income of $14, primarily foreign exchange gains, offset by net interest expense of $3.

Total other income was $1,119 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $11 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The total for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 includes a net non-cash gain of $2,494 from the change in fair value of contingent consideration, partially offset by $1,379 in net interest expense related to the accounts receivable financing facilities and other obligations, primarily those of TVS, and other income of $4.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: The Company recorded income tax expense of $155 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and $427 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $3 for both the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. The tax expense for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 reflects current tax obligations arising from the foreign operations of 42 Telecom in Malta and Sweden. The tax expense for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025 relates to 42 Telecom for the period from August 1, 2025, the date of its acquisition.

net.heading: Net Loss
net.text:
Net loss was $3,370 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $965 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, representing an increase in net loss of $2,405. The increase was driven primarily by a non-cash loss of $1,478 from the change in fair value of contingent consideration, compared to none in the prior-year period, and by higher net interest expense of $494, together with increased operating expenses associated with the Company’s expanded operations, partially offset by gross profit of $3,316 generated by the telecommunications subsidiaries, compared to $710 in the prior-year period. Total comprehensive loss was $3,331 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, which includes $39 of foreign currency translation income.

Net loss was $5,388 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $2,111 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, representing an increase in net loss of $3,277. The increase was driven primarily by higher operating expenses associated with the Company’s expanded operations following the consolidation of TVS and the inclusion of 42 Telecom for the full nine-month period, together with net interest expense of $1,379, which more than offset gross profit of $8,785, compared to $710 in the prior-year period, and a net non-cash gain from the change in fair value of contingent consideration of $2,494.

ocf.heading: Cash Used in Operating Activities
ocf.text:
Net cash used in operating activities was $1,581 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $503 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Despite reporting a net loss of $5,388, operating cash outflow was limited to $1,581 due to non-cash charges, including $5,948 in amortization of intangible assets, $3,291 in amortization of prepaid expenses, $583 in stock-based compensation expense, $529 in provision for expected credit losses, $53 in amortization of right of use assets, and $40 in depreciation, partially offset by a $2,494 non-cash gain from the change in fair value of contingent consideration.

Working capital movements during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 were substantial but largely offsetting, reflecting the high-volume, low-margin nature of our international voice termination carrier operations. Accounts receivable, before the provision for expected credit losses of $529, increased by $165,658 on a cash flow basis ($165,129 net of the provision), driven by TVS’s international voice termination billing cycles, where large volumes of traffic are invoiced to carriers on monthly payment terms. This increase was substantially offset by an increase of $158,042 in accounts payable, reflecting the parallel payment terms on the supplier side of the VoIP carrier business.

da.heading: Depreciation and Amortization
da.text: Depreciation and amortization was $1,996 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and $5,988 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. Depreciation and amortization was $644 for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, consisting of amortization of $636 and depreciation of $8, which has been reclassified from selling, general and administrative expenses to conform to the current-period presentation. The increase reflects amortization of identifiable intangible assets recognized in connection with the acquisitions of 42 Telecom and Telvantis Voice Services, Inc. and the Eliznikcomp OÜ asset purchase, as well as depreciation of property, plant and equipment acquired through the 42 Telecom acquisition. Amortization of intangible assets was $1,984 and depreciation of property, plant and equipment was $12 for the three months ended September 30, 2026; amortization of intangible assets was $5,948 and depreciation of property, plant and equipment was $40 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

sbc.text: Net cash used in operating activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 was primarily due to our net loss of $2,111, partially offset by non-cash expenses of $1,513, primarily stock-based compensation of $857 and amortization of intangible assets of $636, and net cash provided by changes in operating assets and liabilities of $95, reflecting the inclusion of 42 Telecom from August 1, 2025.

wc.heading: Related Party Working Capital Advance
wc.text:
On July 20, 2026, Jenifer Osterwalder, the Company’s President and Chief Executive Officer and a member of the Board of Directors, entered into a promissory note with the Company for working capital advances, bearing interest at 4% per annum with a fixed 90-day term maturing October 18, 2026. The Board of Directors approved the arrangement as a related party transaction on July 22, 2026. As of September 30, 2026, $110 had been advanced under the note.

On October 12, 2026, the Board of Directors approved, as a related party transaction, a new promissory note under which Ms. Osterwalder may advance up to $200, bearing interest at 4.00% per annum and maturing on November 30, 2026, subject to extension to March 1, 2027. As of date of these financial statements, $60 had been advanced under the new note.

Formation of Spectral Digital Infrastructure Inc.

On August 19, 2026, the Company formed Spectral Digital Infrastructure Inc., a wholly owned Delaware subsidiary. The subsidiary had no operations and no significant assets or liabilities as of September 30, 2026.

The revenue growth between periods reflects the consolidation of TVS following its acquisition and the inclusion of 42 Telecom for the full three-month period in 2026, compared with two months in 2025.

Total revenues, including related party revenues, were $865,884 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $3,139 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, for the same reasons. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, revenues consisted of voice termination revenues from TVS of $853,288, messaging and platform revenues from 42 Telecom Ltd.

intro.text: Spectral Capital Corporation is a publicly traded technology company that operates as a hybrid research, intellectual property, and operating business. Spectral has operated continuously as an operating company; however, for much of its history, the Company’s operations were relatively small in scale and primarily focused on research and development, software experimentation, and intellectual property creation. While these efforts resulted in the development of proprietary technologies and technical know-how, Spectral’s earlier software products achieved limited commercial adoption and did not generate meaningful recurring revenues.

rd.heading: Research and Development Activities
rd.text:
Spectral plans to continue investing in research and development, with an emphasis on applied technologies that have potential commercial relevance to its operating businesses or target markets. R&D activities are expected to focus on software development, algorithm design, data analytics, and automation tools, rather than speculative or purely theoretical research. Management intends to allocate R&D resources in a disciplined manner, balancing innovation objectives with the need to manage costs and achieve near- and medium-term operational goals.

Certain research initiatives may involve emerging or experimental technologies, including quantum-inspired or hybrid computing approaches. These initiatives are exploratory in nature and may require substantial additional development, validation, and investment before they can be commercialized, if at all. The Company’s plan of operations does not assume that any specific R&D initiative will result in commercially viable products.

The 2025 tax benefit reflects the net effect of foreign income taxes in Malta and Sweden on 42 Telecom’s profitable operations, offset by a U.S. federal deferred tax benefit arising from the recognition of deferred tax liabilities in connection with the business combinations.

net.heading: Net Income
net.text: Net income was $918,355 for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to net loss of $(3,270,544) for the year ended December 31, 2024, representing an improvement of $4,188,899. The improvement was driven by the revenue and gross profit contributions from 42 Telecom’s operations and the non-cash gain from the change in fair value of contingent consideration, partially offset by increased operating expenses associated with the Company’s expanded operations and corporate infrastructure. Total comprehensive income was $1,050,906 for the year ended December 31, 2025, which includes $132,551 of foreign currency translation gains.

net sales.text: For the year ended December 31, 2025, two customers individually accounted for 10% or more of the Company’s consolidated revenues. lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
